correctness.rationale: For an edge subset D of K_n, total domination of J(n,2) is equivalent to at most one isolated underlying vertex and no K2 component. Every nontrivial component uses at least 3 vertices and at least v-1 edges. At the known optimum m=ceil(2(n-1)/3), equality forces an acyclic component profile: P3 blocks, plus only the listed order-4/order-5 exceptional trees. The n mod 3 cases exhaust 0/1 isolated vertices; no other graphs can have m edges. A labelled-tree count via Prüfer sequences produces the exact factorial formula. Direct enumeration of all 10,198,617 candidates for n=4..10 and independent exact profile counts for n=4..100 match the formulas. The infinite proof is analytic, not empirical.

value.rationale: The newly known optimum total-domination number of triangular graphs motivates the precise next problem: how many distinct minimum solutions exist and what are all their underlying structures? The answer is a complete all-order classification and labelled census, with unexpectedly different residue classes and an asymptotically vanishing fraction of non-isolating optima for n divisible by three. The optimum cardinality alone does not imply these facts. This is a natural exact extremal-configuration invariant of an infinite family, rather than a single small computation or unmotivated parameter slice.
